title: Clinical Diagnostic Tool Compliance Framework
business: A health-tech startup developing a diagnostic support application for radiologists.
problem: The startup risks legal liability and regulatory non-compliance by failing to enforce usage restrictions and failing to obtain necessary Health Regulatory Authorizations when distributing their AI-enhanced diagnostic model.
solution: By adopting the Health AI Developer Foundations (HAI-DEF) terms, the startup establishes a formal compliance pipeline that mandates the inclusion of specific use restrictions in all downstream agreements and ensures that any model derivative undergoes rigorous regulatory review before distribution.
steps: Integrate the HAI-DEF Terms of Use into the startup's end-user license agreement (EULA) for all downstream clinical partners.
Implement a mandatory notification system that alerts third-party recipients that the model is subject to HAI-DEF restrictions.
Conduct a regulatory assessment to determine if the specific diagnostic application requires Health Regulatory Authorization.
Attach the required Notice text file to all non-hosted distributions of the model derivatives.
Maintain a clear audit trail of all modifications to the base model to ensure compliance with attribution requirements.
outcome: The startup achieves a transparent, legally defensible distribution model that mitigates the risk of being classified as an unauthorized medical device manufacturer.
limitation: A significant tradeoff is the potential for Google to remotely restrict usage if they reasonably believe the service violates the agreement, which could cause sudden service outages for clinical users. Developers must monitor their usage patterns against the Prohibited Use Policy to prevent such interruptions.
